Agent Name: Planner
Step Number: 1
Reason for Mistake: The Planner made a fundamental conceptual error in defining the "smallest unit" that retains the characteristics of an element. It incorrectly concluded that the nucleus is the smallest unit, failing to recognize that while the nucleus determines the element's identity (atomic number), the "characteristics of copper" (including its chemical properties, reactivity, and electrical conductivity) are emergent properties of the entire atom (nucleus + electron cloud). An isolated nucleus does not exhibit the chemical or physical behaviors associated with copper metal. The correct answer is the atom, as it is the smallest unit that retains the full set of elemental characteristics.
